landing.heroTitle: The right specialist, at any hour.
landing.heroBody: Describe what's wrong and get pointed to the right specialisation. Book a slot that actually suits you — overnight included — and consult over secure video. Your prescriptions and reports stay in one place afterwards.
landing.trustNote: Registering takes a minute. Every doctor is verified by an administrator before patients can book them.
landing.step1Body: Type your symptoms in your own words. The checker suggests which specialisation fits and how urgent it looks. Skip it and browse doctors directly if you already know.
landing.step2Title: Pick a doctor and a time
landing.step2Body: Filter by specialisation, language and fee. Each doctor publishes their own hours, so every slot you see is one they will be there for.
landing.step3Body: The call opens from the appointment itself, ten minutes before it starts. Chat and any reports you have shared sit beside the video.
landing.step4Body: The doctor issues it during or after the call. It arrives in your history as a PDF, next to every report you have uploaded.
landing.sosBody: One tap shows the ambulance number, maps the nearest hospitals in order of distance, and emails your emergency contact your live location.
landing.recordsBody: Upload lab reports and scans once. A doctor can open them only while you have an appointment with them, through a link that expires in minutes.
landing.langBody: Use the whole platform in the language you think in — including the answers the symptom checker gives you.
landing.specialtiesBody: The number beside each field is how many verified doctors are currently practising in it.
landing.emergencyTitle: In an emergency, don't book — call.
landing.emergencyBody: MedConsult schedules consultations; it is not an emergency service. For a medical emergency in India, call {{number}} for an ambulance.
landing.disclaimer: MedConsult is an academic project built to demonstrate a telemedicine workflow. It is not a certified medical device or a regulated healthcare service. Prescriptions generated here are for demonstration only and are not legally valid e-prescriptions. In a real emergency, call your local emergency number immediately.

symptoms.placeholder: For example: I have had a dry cough and a mild fever for four days, and my chest feels tight when I climb stairs.
symptoms.detailHint: The more detail you give, the more useful the suggestion.
symptoms.duration: How many days has this been going on?
symptoms.urgencyHint_emergency: Your description includes something that needs immediate medical attention.
symptoms.urgencyHint_urgent: You should be seen today or tomorrow rather than waiting.
symptoms.urgencyHint_routine: This is worth a consultation, but does not appear to be an emergency.
symptoms.urgencyHint_self_care: Rest and monitor. Book a consultation if it does not improve or gets worse.
symptoms.conditionsHint: These are possibilities to discuss with a doctor, not a diagnosis.
symptoms.languageWarning: Our emergency keyword checks currently work best in English. Your description was assessed, but if you are seriously unwell please use the emergency page rather than relying on this result.

sos.title: Emergency
sos.subtitle: Call for help, find the nearest hospital, and alert your emergency contact.
sos.callAmbulanceHint: If this is a medical emergency, call first. Everything else on this page can wait.
sos.noContact: You have not saved an emergency contact, so there is nobody for us to alert.
sos.willAlert: We will alert {{name}}{{relation}} with your name, the time, and your location.
sos.confirmWithLocation: Your contact will receive an email with your current location. Only do this in a real emergency.
sos.confirmNoLocation: Your location is not available, so the alert will be sent without it. Only do this in a real emergency.
sos.emailNotSent: The email could not be sent: {{reason}}
sos.stillCall: This alert does not call an ambulance. Dial {{number}} yourself if you need one.
sos.geo_denied: Location access was refused. You can still send an alert and call for help, but your contact will not receive your location.
sos.geo_unavailable: Your location could not be determined. Check that location services are switched on.
sos.geo_timeout: Finding your location took too long. Try again, or continue without it.
sos.geo_unsupported: This browser does not support location services.
sos.noHospitals: We could not find any hospital within {{km}} km of you. Do not wait — call the ambulance service, they will know where to take you.
sos.fallbackExplained: The live hospital map could not be reached, so these are well-known hospitals from our built-in list rather than a live search. Distances are real, but there may be closer hospitals we could not see.
sos.osmAttribution: Hospital data and map tiles © OpenStreetMap contributors.

profile.subtitle: Your details, medical history and emergency contact.
profile.medicalHint: Doctors you consult can see this. Allergies in particular are shown prominently on any prescription.
profile.allergiesHint: For example: Penicillin, Sulfa drugs, Peanuts
profile.emergencyHint: This is who we alert when you press the emergency button. Without it, the SOS screen has nobody to notify.
profile.whatsappHint: Digits only, including the country code and no plus sign. For example 919876543210.
profile.whatsappOptInTitle: Your contact needs to opt in once — the key is issued to them, not to us
profile.whatsappStep1: Ask them to save {{number}} in their phone contacts.
profile.whatsappStep2: From WhatsApp, they send it this exact message:
profile.whatsappStep3: CallMeBot replies within about two minutes with a short numeric key. Enter that key above. If nothing arrives, the service is busy — wait and try again later.
profile.whatsappOpenOptIn: Open the opt-in message in WhatsApp
profile.whatsappCaveat: CallMeBot is a free community service, not an official WhatsApp integration. It is rate-limited and intended for personal use, so treat it as a convenience rather than something to rely on. Email remains the primary alert channel.
profile.twilioOptInTitle: Your contact needs to join the WhatsApp sandbox once
profile.twilioStep1: Ask them to save the sandbox number shown in your Twilio console (usually +1 415 523 8886).
profile.twilioStep2: From WhatsApp, they send it the join code from that same console page, for example: join olive-tiger
profile.twilioStep3: Twilio replies to confirm. From then on they will receive alerts — no key to enter here.
profile.twilioCaveat: This is Twilio's free WhatsApp sandbox. It is reliable but shared, so messages arrive from a generic Twilio number and each recipient must join once. A production deployment would use an approved WhatsApp sender instead.
profile.whatsappOff: WhatsApp alerts are currently switched off on the server, so only email will be sent. The number is saved and will be used if the channel is enabled later.

availability.subtitle: Publish the hours you accept consultations. Patients can only book inside these windows.
availability.overnightHint: There is no restriction on the time of day. To offer overnight hours such as 22:00–02:00, add one window ending at 24:00 and another starting at 00:00 on the next day.
availability.timezoneNote: Windows are saved in your timezone ({{zone}}) and shown to patients in theirs.
availability.confirmDeleteWindow: Remove this availability window? Appointments already confirmed inside it are not cancelled.
availability.blockedHint: Block individual days for leave or holidays without changing your weekly schedule.
availability.alwaysOnBody: You are accepting appointments at every hour of every day, including overnight. Patients can book any slot they like.
availability.alwaysOffBody: Turn this on to accept appointments at any hour, on all seven days. It replaces the weekly windows below.
